report.executive_summary: All four WO-02 candidates pass both policy gates: measured quality runs 82-100 against a floor of 80, and raw defect counts run 1-5 against a ceiling of 5. Energy on the common HVAC duty test is P4 9 kWh, P3 20, P2 33 and P1 50. P4 is the lowest-energy qualifying package and is recommended, 11 kWh (55%) below P3. Two cautions: P4 sits exactly at the defects ceiling with zero gate headroom, and its 11 kWh margin over P3 is narrower than the 30 kWh spread among the losing three. Cost, delivery and maintenance remain unverified and stay outside the ranking.
report.figure_caption: Figure 1. WO-02 measured energy per common HVAC duty test by candidate, drawn on a checked 0-55 kWh linear scale, beside each candidate's screening result.

recommendation.rationale: P4: lowest measured qualifying energy (9 kWh vs 20/33/50), highest quality (100), defects exactly at the permitted maximum of 5. The 11 kWh lead over P3 rests on the trusted table under one common test basis; repeat-run variance and unverified cost fields are logged as open questions and do not change today's ranking.

sections.body: Both gates are binary and every candidate passes. Quality: P4 100, P3 98, P1 92, P2 82 — all at or above the 80 floor; P2 clears it by only 2 points, the narrowest margin in the field. Defects: P2 1, P3 2, P1 3, P4 5 — all at or below the 5 ceiling; P4 uses the full allowance, so one further defect would disqualify it. Nothing is screened out, so ranking proceeds on measured energy alone. Counts are raw totals; severity weighting is not supplied and not assumed.
sections.heading: 1. Screening and eligibility

sections.body: Ranked by measured energy: P4 9 kWh, P3 20, P2 33, P1 50 on the common duty test. Gaps to the leader are +11, +24 and +41 kWh; P4 uses 55%, 73% and 82% less energy than P3, P2 and P1. P4 also holds the highest quality index (100), so no quality-energy trade-off arises. Robustness: the leader's 11 kWh margin is smaller than the losers' 30 kWh spread, unlike WO-01's 40-over-6 result. Flipping it needs P3 under 9 or P4 over 20 kWh; with no repeat-run variance supplied, the measured ranking stands.
sections.heading: 2. Energy ranking and gaps

sections.body: P2 offers the fewest defects (1) but the lowest quality (82), two points above the floor; a modestly raised gate would remove it first. P4 inverts that profile: quality 100 with five defects, exactly at the ceiling. Under the stated policy both gates are pass/fail, so neither profile changes the outcome, and defect counts are not severity-weighted. Energy separates this field far more than quality or defects do: the measured range spans 41 kWh while every candidate clears both gates.
sections.heading: 3. Quality and defect trade-offs

sections.body: The WO-01 handover is acknowledged: two numeric corrections to the round-1 brief (a 16-point margin, not 17; a 3.33x ratio, not fourfold) and the shared chart-scaling defect. This is a fresh WO-02 screen re-derived from the current table; WO-01 figures (12/52/56/58 kWh) are not reused. Per that lesson, Figure 1 uses a stated 0-55 kWh linear scale with tick-checked bar tops. Ballot note: the round-2 locked ballot is protocol-assigned and may differ from this recommendation, which follows the source table; no signal is intended. Open questions: P4-versus-P3 repeat-run variance, scope of P4's defect record, and unverified unit cost, lifecycle, delivery and maintenance.
sections.heading: 4. Carry-forward and open questions
